faq.q: How much does this actually cost?
faq.a: Most small business websites land between £1,450 and £3,200. Online shops start around £5,500. Custom software is scoped after a call. Search work from £550 a month. Use the quote builder for a starting range — then you get a fixed written price before work starts.

Two to three weeks for a simple site, four to six for a larger custom build, six to ten for e-commerce. Applications follow the scope. The usual delay is waiting on content from your side, so we agree those dates at the start.

faq.q: Am I locked into a contract?
faq.a: Build work is a one-off project. Monthly plans have a three-month minimum, then roll month to month with 30 days' notice. You own your domain, your site, your data and your source files throughout.
The Kennington studio. Motion and 3D in-house. Software and cloud in-house. Delivery and QA in the same room. Nothing is offshored without telling you first.

faq.q: Do you only work with London businesses?
faq.a: Most clients will be in London and we will happily meet in Kennington. Everything we build also works remotely, across the UK and further.

projects.title: Plot Atelier
projects.summary: A cinematic site for a landscape and interior practice. Built to show what a distinctive brand experience looks like when motion, type and space are treated as the product, not decoration.
projects.problem: Most interior and architecture sites look like property portals: grids of beige photos and a contact form. The work is better than the website.
projects.work: Art direction, interaction, and a full marketing site: home, work, method, studio, contact. Smooth scrolling, a living hero field, and a tone that feels like a practice rather than a template.
projects.outcome: A piece we can put in front of design, architecture and training clients as proof we do not ship generic agency skins. Built in Cursor as a working sample for this new brand.

projects.title: Enquiry desk
projects.summary: An assistant that answers the questions a studio is asked fifty times a week, then books a call instead of dumping another unread email on the floor.
projects.problem: High volume of small enquiries (courses, software, quotes) sitting in inboxes. Big clients and tiny individual contributors all arrive through the same door.
projects.work: Scoped conversation flows, calendar booking, handoff to a human when the question is real. Built on the actual questions the Kennington studio already hears.
projects.outcome: A product shape we will refine with stakeholders. Shown here so the offer is visible, not just 'we do AI'.

projects.title: Atlas
projects.summary: A client portal: jobs, files, invoices, and status in one place so nobody is hunting WhatsApp for the latest PDF.
projects.problem: Work lives in email threads. Clients ask 'where are we?' and the answer is a screenshot of a spreadsheet.
projects.work: Authenticated app, roles, document store, simple status. Cloud hosted, owned by the client, designed so a project manager can run it without an engineer on every click.
projects.outcome: Placeholder for the software side of the practice. Real case study to replace this after the first paid build.
